Maya (sec): FYI we just received a DSAR for a customer in Private that uses a customer-managed KMS in EU-west. Their ticket says retention exception was set for 3 days last month to allow a compliance export. Legal says that exception is expired. Can we verify end-to-end delete runway for that tenant?
Ravi (infra): Quick check: do we still have any cross-region snapshot replicas for that tenant? Backups could keep ciphertext around.
Diego (eng): Yes there's a snapshot in us-central created during the export window. Deleting objects requires KMS unwrapping or key destruction from the customer side. We don't possess the plaintext keys.
Priya (privacy): Legal confirmation first: we need an explicit "no hold" email. Legal Ops?
Legal Ops: Confirmed — no active holds. Export exception expired on 2026-02-05. We need a deletion receipt showing what objects were removed and an audit bundle proving the KMS signature for authorization.
Maya (sec): Okay. Proposed flow: 1) create an ephemeral principal with minimal read access to keystore metadata and snapshot manifests; 2) erasure worker requests a Delegated Delete Token (DDT) signed by customer's KMS via privpath; 3) erasure worker executes removal and emits an audit bundle.
Diego (eng): For the ephemeral principal, suggest `ephemeral:erasure@priv` minted by breakglass. Policy: allow `privpath.keystore.read`, `privpath.snapshots.list`, `privpath.delete.requestDDT`. TTL 10m. Must require a manual approval step in runbook.
Ravi (infra): I'll add a helper that mints the principal and sets the condition binding to `request.auth.principal == "admin-oncall"`. Example ACL snippet we can call from runbook:
```json
{"bindings": [{"role":"roles/privpath.eraser","members":["serviceAccount:ephemeral-erasure@redwood.iam"],"condition":{"expression":"request.time < timestamp(\"2026-05-01T00:00:00Z\")"}}]}
```
Maya (sec): Also require that the mint logs include the operator ticket ID and approver's username. No silent minting.
Priya (privacy): Audit fields we need in the final bundle: `subject_id`, `tenant_id`, `snapshot_ids_removed` (hashes OK), `DDT_id`, `keystore_thumbprint`, `operator`, `policy_version`, `pre_delete_snapshot_count`, `post_delete_snapshot_count`. Bundle must be signed by our audit service and stored in the retention-audit bucket with SSE-KMS.
Diego (eng): Add that we should not store the raw KMS key ARN in the stored audit. Store a truncated fingerprint and the DDT signature metadata only. Also log verification steps: `ddt_signature_validated=true` and `ddt_expiry` timestamp.
erasure-bot: New erasure job 99012 created -> waiting for no-hold confirmation and RBAC minting. (:eyes:)
Ravi (infra): Edge case: what if the customer's KMS accepts the DDT request but refuses to sign delete because of tenant policy? Then erasure should mark the job `blocked-kms-policy` and notify Legal + Customer Support. Do not attempt removal of snapshots without KMS signature.
Legal Ops: Agreed. If customer-side manual deletion happens, we need a signed email from their KMS admin or a console screenshot plus trace id to mark as complete.
Maya (sec): Security check: ensure the ephemeral principal can't call `privpath.key.rotate` or `privpath.key.create`. Limit to read + request DDT only. Diego, please run a quick vault policy audit and open a vuln if there's any broader scope.
Diego (eng): Will scan policies now. If anything risky, I'll open SEC-1122 and include a diff of current bindings.
Priya (privacy): Also: retention exception history must be included in the audit bundle (dates, rationale) so Legal can reconcile the timeline.
Ravi (infra): I'll add a runbook step to reconcile retention_exception logs for the tenant and attach them to the bundle. Also scripting snippet to mint ephemeral role:
```bash
# mint ephemeral erasure SA
redwoodctl iam grant --service-account ephemeral-erasure@redwood.iam \
  --role roles/privpath.eraser --ttl 600 --reason "DSAR erase - ticket 7834" --approver $ONCALL
```
Maya (sec): Good. One more: require a vuln triage before any new minting path goes live. If the triage finds a possible elevation path via token-broker, pause and escalate to Sec Eng.
Diego (eng): Triage in progress. If OK, I'll add an allowlist in token-broker to restrict who can request the ephemeral erasure SA.
erasure-bot: Erasure job 99012 status -> pending RBAC approval (ONCALL_APPROVAL).
Legal Ops: I'll attach the "no hold" confirmation to ticket 7834 and add guidance to request customer proof if KMS cannot sign.
Priya (privacy): I'll prepare a deletion receipt template that includes the audit bundle hash and DDT_id but redacts any PII. Will post to privacy drive and link in the ticket.
Ravi (infra): PR #4280 created for runbook and mint helper. Includes `--ttl` enforcement and attaching operator metadata.
Maya (sec): Summary: legal no-hold confirmed; infra to provide ephemeral SA with 10m TTL and strict policy; erasure worker to request DDT signed by customer KMS; audit bundle fields agreed; triage/vuln check on minting path. Followups: @Diego to finish policy audit, @Ravi to merge runbook PR, @Priya to post receipt template.
Diego (eng): On it.
Ravi (infra): Will merge after unit tests.
Priya (privacy): Template posted and linked in ticket 7834.
Maya (sec): If anything blocks the delete start, mark thread with `blocked-dsar` and escalate. Thanks all.
